title: Part One, Chapter 3: The Destruction of the Men of Wood

verses.t: And afterwards all these men of wood were finished off, destroyed and killed. It was decided by the Heart of the Sky, and a great flood was made that came upon them. The flesh of the men was of cork wood; of that material they were made and carved by the Creator; and the women were made of the pith of reeds, for that was the Creator's will, to make them of that material. But they did not remember or thank the Creator who had created them, for having created them, and so they were killed and drowned. A great resin and pitch came down from the sky, and a bird called Xecotcovuch came and gouged out their eyes; another came, called Camulotz, and cut off their heads; another animal came, called Cotzbalam, and ate their flesh; and the one called Tucumbalam broke their bones and sinews, and they were ground into meal. And this was in punishment and as a warning, because they had given no thanks before their mother and father and Lord, the Heart of the Sky, who is called Huracán. And because of them the face of the earth grew dark, and a drizzling rain began, night and day; and every kind of animal, small and great, came, and the sticks and the stones, and struck them in the face and shamed them. And everything spoke: the grinding stones, the griddles, the plates, the bowls, the pots, the dogs and the water jars; all that there were insulted them and said to them, "You treated us very badly; you bit us, and so now we shall bite you," said the dogs. And the hens and the grinding stones said, "We were greatly tormented by all of you, every day, at evening and at morning, always going 'holi, holi, huqui, huqui'" (that is the sound of the stone and the hiss it makes in grinding). "This was our labour for your faces, so that you might be well liked; and since you were not, now you shall feel our strength: we shall grind your flesh and make meal of your bodies." This is what the grinding stones said to them. And the dogs spoke and said, "Because you never gave us our food, but we could only watch you, and you chased us and threw us out, and a stick was always ready to beat us while you were eating; that is how you treated us, because we could not speak. Perhaps you would not be dying now if you had looked to yourselves. That is how we were lost; now you shall taste the teeth that are in our mouths; we shall eat you," said the dogs, throwing it in their faces. And the griddles and the pots spoke to them in this way: "You gave us pain and suffering; our mouths and our faces are blackened with soot; we were always cooking over the fire; you burned us and we felt the pain. Now you shall taste it, and we shall burn you," said the pots, all throwing it in their faces. And the hearth stones spoke with fury: "Let the fire come! Our heads were set under the pot; you made us do it, and you caused us pain." And the men ran about in confusion. They tried to climb up onto the houses, and the houses fell down under them and brought them down; they tried to climb the trees, and the trees threw them off; they tried to get into the caves, and the caves closed up before them. And so they were all destroyed, annihilated and put to shame. And so it is said that the sign of this people is the monkeys that now go about in the forests; that is why they were left as a sign, because they were only of wood, made by the Creator; and that is why the monkey looks like man, because it is the sign of another kind of men, made of wood.
